name: CUBRID
tagline: Korean open-source RDBMS with built-in HA and Oracle-like SQL, common in Korean public sector.
description: CUBRID is an open-source relational database developed in South Korea, originally at NHN and now by CUBRID Corporation. It offers a three-tier architecture (broker, server, client), built-in high availability with automatic failover, and SQL that borrows heavily from Oracle conventions such as hierarchical queries, synonyms and MERGE, which eases migrations from Oracle in Korean government and enterprise projects. The engine is Apache 2.0 and connectors are BSD, and the 11.x line receives frequent patch releases. Outside Korea its community, tooling and documentation are thin.

pricing.notes: Free; CUBRID Corporation sells technical support and migration services.

scale.notes: HA via master/slave replication with broker failover; sharding via CUBRID SHARD is application-assisted.

strengths: Built-in HA with heartbeat-based automatic failover
Oracle-style SQL features ease Oracle migrations
Broker layer provides connection pooling and load balancing
Permissive Apache 2.0 license for the engine
Proven in large Korean web and public-sector deployments
weaknesses: Small international community; much documentation is Korean-first
Few third-party tools, ORMs and managed services
No native full-text or vector search
Limited cloud presence outside Korean providers
useCases: Web services needing built-in HA without extra tooling
notIdealFor: Teams relying on mainstream ecosystem tooling
